title: feat: add concat_mla_kv_quant_fp8, a fused MLA context K/V pack with saturating fp8 cast
body:
<!-- .github/pull_request_template.md -->

## 📌 Description

Kimi-K3 and DeepSeek-style MLA models prefill long contexts in chunks. For every chunk of every MLA layer, the model projects the gathered latent cache into per-head keys and values, casts them to FP8, and lays them out as the contiguous key and value tensors the attention kernel expects (`trtllm_ragged_attention_deepseek` with separate Q/K/V).

Today that cast-and-layout step is done by four separate PyTorch operations: two FP8 casts and two strided slice copies. On the deployment that motivated this work (Kimi-K3 FP4, TP8 x DCP8 on two GB300 nodes, FP8 KV cache, an agentic-coding replay at 70 concurrent sessions), that tail costs about 380 microseconds and moves 879 MB per 66k-token chunk, for each of 24 MLA layers, on almost every engine step.

vLLM already ships a private fused kernel for this step (`fused_kimi_k3_mla_kv_concat_quant_fp8`, added in vllm-project/vllm#51772), and vllm-project/vllm#56881 routes vLLM's decode-context-parallel path through it. That fixes the problem for vLLM only. This PR adds an equivalent fused kernel to FlashInfer as a public, head-generic API so that vLLM, SGLang and any other FlashInfer consumer can call one library function instead of each carrying its own copy. FlashInfer's existing `concat_mla_k` cannot serve this case: it requires 128 heads and does not cast.

### What this PR adds

One new public function:

```python
key, value = flashinfer.concat_mla_kv_quant_fp8(kv_nope, k_pe, key=None, value=None, *, nope_dim=128)
```

- `kv_nope`: bf16 `[T, H, 256]`, the `kv_b_proj` output laid out as `[k_nope | v]`.
- `k_pe`: bf16 `[T, 64]`, the RoPE'd key shared by all heads.
- Returns `key`: float8_e4m3fn `[T, H, 192]` = `[k_nope | k_pe broadcast]`, and `value`: float8_e4m3fn `[T, H, 128]` = `v`.

The kernel reads the projection output once and writes both outputs in a single launch. One warp handles one token; the RoPE row is converted once per token and broadcast to every head. The head count `H` is a runtime argument; `H = 12` (Kimi-K3's 96 heads split over TP8) gets a fully unrolled fast path, every other head count uses the same kernel with runtime loops. Head dimensions are fixed at 128 / 64 / 128.

**Numerics are unchanged.** The FP8 cast is the same saturating conversion torch uses for `Tensor.to(float8_e4m3fn)` on GPU (round to nearest even, overflow clamps to +/-448, NaN maps to 0x7F). The output is byte-identical to the four-operation path; all 65536 bf16 input patterns were checked.

### When it activates, and how it falls back

The fused kernel runs only when all of the following hold. Any miss takes a plain PyTorch fallback that produces the same bytes, and the reason is counted so it can be inspected.

- Inputs are bf16, contiguous and 16-byte aligned; head dimensions are 128 / 64 / 128.
- The shape is inside the shipped allowlist (`flashinfer/mla_kv_pack_fp8_workloads.json`): compute capability 10.0 or newer, 1 to 128 heads, 1 to 131072 tokens.
- The call is not the first JIT build under CUDA-graph capture.
- `FLASHINFER_SPECIALIZED_KERNEL_DISABLE=1` is not set. Setting it forces the fallback and is the kill switch for A/B testing.

A one-line log message is emitted on the first fused dispatch, and `flashinfer.mla_kv_pack._concat_mla_kv_quant_fp8_stats()` reports call and fallback counts.

**This PR dispatches nothing by itself.** No framework calls the new function until it is wired in. A separate PR needs to be made to wire vLLM to use this FI function.

### Performance

**Kernel-level A/B on GB300**, run inside the vLLM deployment container (CUDA 13.0, torch 2.13), comparing this kernel against vLLM's fused kernel compiled in the same job. Cold L2 per call, one call per CUDA graph, 200 timed iterations.

| chunk size (tokens) | calls per step | this kernel | vLLM fused kernel | speedup |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 66048 | 936 | 101.1 us | 119.5 us | 1.18x |
| 33792 | 24 | 56.3 us | 65.5 us | 1.16x |
| 9344 | 24 | 20.9 us | 25.3 us | 1.22x |
| 1536 | 24 | 9.6 us | 10.1 us | 1.06x |
| all 18 serving shapes, geomean | | | | **1.17x** |

Every serving shape is faster than vLLM's kernel; all 23 measured rows are byte-exact on the fused path, the fallback path and vLLM's kernel. Against the four-operation PyTorch path the fused kernel is about 5.7x faster, but that is not the production comparison since vLLM already runs its own fused kernel on this path.

**End-to-end A/B**, Kimi-K3 FP4 on two GB300 nodes (TP8 x DCP8, FP8 KV cache), 3600-second agentic-coding replay at 70 concurrent sessions, same build on both sides except for the FlashInfer install and one environment variable. Against the stock four-operation path (what upstream vLLM runs today):

| metric at 70 concurrent sessions | stock path | this kernel | change |
|---|---|---|---|
| p90 inter-token latency | 136.4 ms | 126.3 ms | -7.4% |
| p90 normalized interactivity (tokens/s per user) | 6.62 | 7.32 | +10.7% |
| output tokens/s | 694.4 | 690.4 | -0.6% (within noise) |
| mean inter-token latency | 97.7 ms | 97.9 ms | +0.2% (within noise) |

Two runs of identical code on this route differ by about 5% in throughput but only about 2% in p90 inter-token latency and 4% in p90 interactivity, so the tail-latency gains are well outside noise while the throughput and mean-latency changes are not. That is the expected shape of the win: the per-chunk cost this removes matters most on long multi-chunk requests, which populate the latency tail.

Against vLLM's own fused kernel: neutral within noise on every metric. Swapping vLLM's kernel for this one costs nothing at the serving point; the kernel-level gain of about 18 us per chunk call is roughly 1.3 ms of a 93 ms step, below what one replay can resolve.

### Accuracy

Standard probes such as GSM8K use prompts far shorter than the scheduler chunk and never reach the chunked-context path, so we ran a paired teacher-forced perplexity test on long inputs: ten public-domain texts of roughly 30k to 36k tokens each, 330,944 tokens in total, scored token by token on a server using this kernel and a server with the kill switch set. Logs confirm which path each server took.

| | this kernel | stock path |
|---|---|---|
| perplexity | 1.014815 | 1.014815 |
| paired difference | 0.0000% | |
| top-1 token flips | 0 of 330,944 | |
| GSM8K spot check (20 questions, sanity only) | 20/20 | 20/20 |

The two runs are bit-identical, as expected for a kernel whose output is byte-identical to the path it replaces.

### Scope and limitations

- Measurements were taken on `release-v0.6.17` and the branch was then rebased to `main`. The perf results have not been rerun on the rebased head, though we expect no changes since the kernel itself is byte-identical.
- The fused path is enabled only for compute capability 10.0 and newer (Blackwell). Older parts take the PyTorch fallback.
- The FP8 conversion is written with the f32-source form of the PTX `cvt` instruction so it assembles with CUDA 13.0, which the deployment container ships. The bf16x2-source form does not build there.
- Measured on one configuration: GB300, TP8 x DCP8, FP8 KV cache, TRTLLM ragged prefill backend.

### Files

`include/flashinfer/mla_kv_pack_fp8.cuh` (kernel), `csrc/mla_kv_pack_fp8.cu` (binding), `flashinfer/jit/mla_kv_pack.py`, `flashinfer/mla_kv_pack.py` (API, guards, fallback, stats), `flashinfer/mla_kv_pack_fp8_workloads.json` (allowlist), `flashinfer/aot.py`, `flashinfer/__init__.py`, `pyproject.toml`, `flashinfer/trace/templates/attention.py`, `docs/api/concat_ops.rst`, `tests/utils/test_concat_mla_kv_quant_fp8.py`, `tests/trace/test_concat_mla_kv_quant_fp8_reference_correctness.py`.

## 🔍 Related Issues

- vllm-project/vllm#51772 (vLLM's private fused kernel for this step)
- vllm-project/vllm#56881 (routes vLLM's DCP path through that kernel)

## 🧪 Tests

- [x] Tests have been added or updated as needed.
- [x] All tests are passing (`unittest`, etc.).

`tests/utils/test_concat_mla_kv_quant_fp8.py` (24 tests) and `tests/trace/test_concat_mla_kv_quant_fp8_reference_correctness.py` pass on an RTX 5080 (sm_120, torch 2.13, CUDA 13):

- Output is byte-identical to the four-operation PyTorch path on all 24 shapes captured from the serving run, plus sampled shapes up to 131072 tokens, with two random seeds each, and the fused kernel is confirmed to have dispatched on every row.
- All 65536 bf16 bit patterns convert identically.
- The kill switch, the allowlist miss path and the CUDA-graph capture guard each route to the fallback.
- The runtime-head-count path is exact for head counts other than 12.
